# Grid List

> A list of rows that can hold their own buttons, links and checkboxes, moved through with the arrow keys and optionally selected.

`<slab-grid-list>` · Data · built on `[role=grid] + rows`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/grid-list/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/grid-list.js';
import 'slab-elements/grid-list.item.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-grid-list label="Files" multiple>
  <slab-grid-list-item label="plan.pdf">
    plan.pdf
    <button type="button">Share</button>
    <a href="/files/plan.pdf">Download</a>
  </slab-grid-list-item>
  <slab-grid-list-item label="site.jpg">
    site.jpg
    <button type="button">Share</button>
    <a href="/files/site.jpg">Download</a>
  </slab-grid-list-item>
</slab-grid-list>
```

Use a Grid List where each item in a list has controls of its own, such as a row of files, each with Share and Download. A Listbox's Options can't hold controls, and a plain list of them puts every control in the Tab order. A Grid List is reached by Tab once, and the arrow keys move between rows and between the controls in a row, as in React Aria's GridList and the APG's grid.

Each row takes the controls in it out of the Tab order with `tabindex="-1"`, Slab's own Checkbox and Copy Button included, so Tab leaves the Grid List rather than stopping at each. Give each row a `label` when it holds controls, so a screenreader reads "plan.pdf" rather than "plan.pdf Share Download".

Rows aren't selected unless `selectable` is set, or `multiple`, which allows more than one and needs no `selectable`. Then a click on a row, but not on a control in it, selects it, and Grid List dispatches "change". A design can draw a check box on `:state(selectable)` and fill it on `:state(selected)`, as the styled one does. It's only shown, since the row is what's selected and what a screenreader says is selected.

## Keyboard

| Key          | What it does                                                                               |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Tab          | Reaches the row focus was last in, or else the first selected or first row, then leaves.   |
| Down, Up     | Moves to the next or previous row, skipping disabled ones, from a row or a control in one. |
| Home, End    | Moves to the first or last row.                                                            |
| Right, Left  | Moves from a row to each of its controls and back to the row. Swapped right to left.       |
| Escape       | Moves from a control back to its row.                                                      |
| A character  | Moves to the next row whose text starts with what's typed.                                 |
| Enter, Space | Selects the row, or toggles it when `multiple`. Does nothing unless rows are selectable.   |

A control that edits text, such as a text `<input>`, keeps its arrow keys,
Home and End, so Escape is the way back to its row. With `multiple`, Shift
with Up or Down moves and toggles, Shift with Space selects from the last
selected row to the focused one, Control or Command with Shift and Home or
End selects from the focused row to the first or last, and Control or
Command with A selects every row, or none.

## Elements

### `<slab-grid-list>`

Import `slab-elements/grid-list.js` to register it.

A Grid List with no visual styles: a `[role=grid]` of rows, Grid List Items, that can hold controls of their own, such as a Checkbox, buttons and links, and that can be selected.

It's a one-column APG grid, like React Aria's GridList. Tab reaches it once, on the row focus was last in, or else on the first selected row, or else on the first. Down and Up move focus between rows, skipping disabled ones, and Home and End, with or without Control or Command, go to the first and last. Right moves from a row to the first control in it, then to each control after that, and back to the row from the last. Left goes the other way. In a right-to-left Grid List, Left and Right swap. Escape moves from a control back to its row. Typing moves to the next row whose text starts with what's typed. A control that edits text, such as a text `<input>`, keeps its arrow keys, Home and End, and so does one that handles a key itself and cancels it.

Rows aren't selected unless `selectable` or `multiple` is set. Then Space, Enter and a click on a row, but not on a control in it, select the row, or toggle it when `multiple`, which makes rows selectable without `selectable`. With `multiple`, Shift with Down or Up moves and toggles, Shift with Space selects every row from the one last selected to the focused one, and Control or Command with Shift and Home or End selects every one from the focused row to the first or last, moving there. Control or Command with A selects every enabled row, or none when they all are already. These are the APG's keys for a multi-select grid.

Put controls in it that take focus themselves, such as `<button>`s, links and Slab's own Checkbox. Each row takes them out of the page's Tab order, so Tab leaves the Grid List rather than stopping at each.

Style it through its part, and each row through its part and states.

#### Attributes

| Name               | Type      | Default | Description                                                                                         |
| ------------------ | --------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` (required) | `string`  |         | Names the grid list.                                                                                |
| `multiple`         | `boolean` | `false` | Whether more than one row can be selected. Rows are selectable when it's set, without `selectable`. |
| `selectable`       | `boolean` | `false` | Whether a row can be selected.                                                                      |

#### Properties

| Name                        | Type                   | Description                         |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `items` (read-only)         | `GridListItem[]`       | Its Grid List Items, in order.      |
| `selectedItem` (read-only)  | `GridListItem \| null` | The first selected item, or `null`. |
| `selectedItems` (read-only) | `GridListItem[]`       | Every selected item, in order.      |

#### Methods

| Signature                             | Description                                     |
| ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `focus(options?: FocusOptions): void` | Focuses it, or the part of it that takes focus. |

#### Events

| Name     | Type    | Description                                                                                            |
| -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `change` | `Event` | When the user changes its value, as a native control's does. Setting it from code doesn't dispatch it. |

#### Slots

| Name      | Type           | Description |
| --------- | -------------- | ----------- |
| (default) | `GridListItem` |             |

#### CSS parts

| Name   | Description |
| ------ | ----------- |
| `grid` | The rows    |

### `<slab-grid-list-item>`

Import `slab-elements/grid-list.item.js` to register it.

A Grid List Item with no visual styles: one row of its Grid List, a `[role=row]` with a single `[role=gridcell]` around what's slotted into it, such as text, a Checkbox, buttons and links.

The row itself takes focus, and its Grid List moves focus between rows with the arrow keys. Left and Right move focus between the row and the controls in it. Those controls are taken out of the page's Tab order, with `tabindex="-1"`, so Tab leaves the Grid List rather than stopping at each.

It's named by its content, or by `label` when that's set, which it should be when there are controls in it, so a screenreader reads "Driveway" rather than "Driveway Details Remove".

Its Grid List sets `:state(active)` on the row focus was last in, and `:state(selectable)` on each row when it has `selectable` or `multiple`, so a design can draw a check box. It sets `:state(disabled)` and `:state(selected)` itself.

#### Attributes

| Name       | Type      | Default | Description                                                                                                                               |
| ---------- | --------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Can't be focused or selected. The controls in it are yours to disable.                                                                    |
| `label`    | `string`  |         | Names the row in place of its content, and is what typeahead matches against.                                                             |
| `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | Like Option's, the attribute is the default state and the property is the current one. Style `:state(selected)` rather than `[selected]`. |

#### Properties

| Name                   | Type            | Description                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `selectable`           | `boolean`       | Set by its Grid List.                                                        |
| `controls` (read-only) | `HTMLElement[]` | What in the row can take focus, in order, other than disabled controls.      |
| `text` (read-only)     | `string`        | What typeahead matches against: its label, or its text when it has no label. |

#### Slots

| Name      | Type                | Description                               |
| --------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| (default) | `Element \| string` | The row's content, and any controls in it |

#### CSS parts

| Name   | Description       |
| ------ | ----------------- |
| `cell` | Holds the content |

#### CSS states

| Name                 | Description                                                                                     |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `:state(active)`     | While it's the active one, which the keyboard moves through while focus stays on its container. |
| `:state(disabled)`   | While it's disabled.                                                                            |
| `:state(selectable)` | While its Grid List is selectable.                                                              |
| `:state(selected)`   | While it's selected.                                                                            |
